# Song of Songs Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 413v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/SNG_003_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** On my bed at night I sought the one my soul loves; I sought him but did not find him. **2** "I will rise now and go about the city, through the streets and the squares; I will seek the one my soul loves." I sought him but did not find him. **3** The watchmen who go about the city found me. "Have you seen the one my soul loves?" **4** Scarcely had I passed them when I found the one my soul loves. I held him and would not let him go until I had brought him to my mother's house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.

**5** I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the does of the field: do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.

**6** What is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all the fragrant powders of the merchant? **7** Behold, it is the litter of Solomon! Sixty warriors surround it, of the warriors of Israel. **8** All of them bearing swords, trained for war, each with his sword at his thigh against the terrors of the night. **9** King Solomon made himself a palanquin from the wood of Lebanon. **10** He made its posts of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple; its interior was inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem. **11** Go out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze upon King Solomon, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, on the day of the gladness of his heart.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Song of Songs 3 — the most explicitly erotic text in the biblical canon. The council reads it as love poetry first, without imposing allegorical frameworks (YHWH-Israel, Christ-Church) that, while historically important, are not intrinsic to the Hebrew text.

---
## Disagreement Log

Minor register variations resolved through standard consensus process.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
